ca_e_maiden_buttress.blurb: Maiden Buttress is a big trad wall on the left skyline of Tahquitz Rock above Idyllwild, at roughly 7,000 feet. It holds a dozen or so routes, all placed with gear, and the range is unusually wide: one easy multi-pitch line in the 5.4 range, a couple of moderate routes, a cluster at 5.10, and a handful of hard 5.12 test pieces. Several climbs run six pitches, while others are short two-pitch cracks. Expect technical crack climbing, some rough and sharp edges, and loose bits to sweep off at the base. The base is reached by scrambling left from the Lunch Rock ledge, and most parties walk off over the top rather than rappel.

ca_east_end.blurb: East End is the eastern tip of The Corridors, a group of rock blades in the Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine, at about 4,700 feet. About a dozen climbs here mix bolted face lines with a few trad cracks, and nearly all of them are modest: a few easy 5.5 to 5.8 routes, a solid block of 5.9 and 5.10, and just one 5.11. The mix of face and crack climbing on short walls makes it a friendly place for building trad skills or clipping bolts on a day in the Eastern Sierra. You arrive via the route into Cattle Pocket, with the Corridors on your right.

ca_ellery_dam_spillway_crag.blurb: A compact crag of about 60 feet near Ellery Lake at roughly 9,500 feet, just off the Tioga Road corridor above Lee Vining. The rock is a jumble of cracks, a dihedral, a roof and an arete, so it is mostly a gear-climbing venue with one short bolted line and one top-rope option. Grades run from easy 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk around 5.10. It is quiet and suits a half-day outing, and the weather at this elevation can turn quickly. Fixed rappel anchors are scarce, so plan to walk off. Part of the west end has collapsed, taking some bolts with it.
ca_ellery_dam_spillway_crag.parking_note: Pull off onto the dirt turnout beside US 120 a short way north of Ellery Dam.

ca_fairway.blurb: Fairway is a single-pitch sport crag in the New Jack City complex of California's High Desert near Barstow, on a hillside just south of the big face of Raven Rocks. Routes are long, around 60 to 70 feet, and the bolting is regarded as dependable. The grades start around 5.9 and are weighted toward 5.11 and 5.12, so it suits climbers who already lead 5.10 comfortably. Much of the day it is shaded, which makes it a good choice when other walls are too hot. Reach it by hiking uphill and south past two neighbouring crags; the ground is uneven, so wear sturdy shoes.

ca_fire_crags.blurb: Fire Crags is a small cluster of boulders above Santa Barbara, in chaparral that was cleared by a wildfire and opened the rocks up to climbers. The routes are short, roughly 20 to 30 feet, bolted and technical, with finger-sized features. Grades span about 5.7 to 5.11, with the largest share at 5.11 and 5.10 and only a few easier lines, so it is better for intermediate to strong climbers than for beginners. Trees give some shade and spots to sit. Weekends can fill the small roadside parking, so an early start helps.
ca_fire_crags.parking_note: Leave the car at the little pull-out on the left at the hairpin bend on Painted Cave Road, about half a mile from Highway 154, or at the larger turnout a bit further up the road.
ca_fire_crags.approach: From the hairpin, a rough foot trail leads to the rocks in about five minutes.

ca_main_wall_right_4.blurb: Main Wall Right is the stretch of tall cliff at The Mill, a basalt rim above Mill Creek Canyon in the Lost Sierra of Northeast California. It lies between the Great Roof and the Alcove and holds about a dozen routes, mostly long, single-pitch sport lines with a few gear routes. Grades run from roughly 5.8 up to a few 5.12s, with the weight in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. The wall catches sun all day, so cloudy or cool days are the better bet. Bring a long rope, as the lowers can be far from the ground. The wall is a short walk from the top of the approach trail.

ca_houda_far_north.blurb: Houda Far North is a cluster of boulders at the north end of the Houda Point beach on the Humboldt coast, the farthest-north of three sectors there. Quality depends on how much sand the beach has: when it is built up, expect slabs, pockets and overhangs, and when it is stripped you can rig short top ropes instead. Thirteen problems range from the easiest grades up to V6, with most in the V0 to V4 band, so beginners have plenty to try. Check the tide before going. Walk down the north stairs to the beach, then head north along the sand for about 250 yards.
ca_houda_far_north.approach: Take the north stairs down to the beach and walk north along the sand for about 250 yards.

ca_grandpa_peabody_boulder.blurb: Grandpa Peabody is the largest boulder in the Peabody group in the Buttermilks, outside Bishop, and one of the best-known blocs in the Eastern Sierra. Its overhanging, tall face carries a small number of problems, and the list is dominated by very hard ones: one problem near V4, then lines from V8 up to V16, with several celebrated hard test pieces. These are tall, committing lines that call for crash pads, spotters and strong skin rather than casual circuits. It is often busy in good weather. From the lower Peabody parking area the boulder is easy to spot and a clear trail leads to it.
